---
title: Teams
icon: UsersRound
description: Group users into teams so a single permission grants a whole group shared access to data.
---

A **team** is Applad's unit of shared access. It answers one question: "these
people, and only these people, may see this." A workspace, a channel, a shared
document, a project board. Instead of listing every user on every row, you name
a team once, and everyone in that team is admitted.

Teams work hand in hand with [permissions](/build/permissions). A row (or file, or
function) whose permissions name a team is reachable by exactly that team's
members. Add someone to the team and they gain access; remove them and they
lose it, with nothing else to update.

Team calls are client-side: they run as the signed-in user (see
[authentication](/build/authentication)). Each request carries the
`x-applad-project: <projectId>` header and, after login, the session bearer
token `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`. The SDK sets both for you.

## Creating a team

Creating a team makes the caller its first, already-joined **owner**. Without
that, the person who made the team would hold no membership and could be locked
out of the very team they just created by its own team-scoped permissions.

```dart
final client = Applad(endpoint: 'https://api.applad.io', projectId: '<projectId>');
// (already signed in, see the authentication guide)

final team = await client.teams.create(name: 'engineering');
final teamId = team['\$id'];
```

`create` takes an optional `teamId` (default `unique()`, a generated ID) and an
optional list of `roles` to record on the creator's owner membership.

```dart
Future<Map<String, dynamic>> create({
  required String name,
  String? teamId,
  List<String>? roles,
});
```

Under the hood this is `POST /v1/teams` with `{ "name": ..., "teamId": ...,
"roles": [...] }`, returning the new team:

```json
{
  "$id": "6f2b...",
  "$createdAt": "2026-07-28T10:00:00Z",
  "$updatedAt": "2026-07-28T10:00:00Z",
  "name": "engineering",
  "total": 0,
  "prefs": {}
}
```

<Callout title="Server-created teams have no owner">
  When a team is created with a server [API key](/build/authentication) (header
  `x-applad-key`) rather than a user session, there is no user to enrol, so the
  team is created with no owner membership. Create teams as the signed-in user
  when you want the creator to be a member.
</Callout>

## Listing teams

```dart
final res = await client.teams.list();
final teams = res['teams']; // List<Map>
final total = res['total']; // int
```

```dart
Future<Map<String, dynamic>> list({ int? limit, int? offset, String? search });
```

What you get back depends on who is asking. This is deliberate:

- A **signed-in user** sees only the teams they have actually joined. They never
  learn the names of other users' teams.
- A **server API key** or **console admin** sees every team in the project.

`limit`, `offset` and `search` (a name substring) page and filter the list. The
underlying route is `GET /v1/teams`, returning `{ "total": <int>, "teams":
[...] }`.

Read one team by ID with `client.teams.get(teamId)` (`GET
/v1/teams/{teamId}`). A single team's `total` field is its count of **joined**
members.

## Renaming and deleting a team

```dart
await client.teams.update(teamId, 'platform');   // PUT /v1/teams/{teamId}
await client.teams.delete(teamId);               // DELETE /v1/teams/{teamId} -> 204
```

## Inviting a member

Invite someone by email. The returned membership carries a one-time `secret`.
Hand that secret to the invitee (as a join link, say) and they redeem it to
join. A self-hosted instance often has no SMTP configured, so Applad returns the
secret to you rather than assuming it can email it.

```dart
final invite = await client.teams.createMembership(
  teamId,
  email: 'grace@example.com',
  roles: ['developer'],
);

final membershipId = invite['\$id'];
final secret = invite['secret']; // present ONLY on this create response
```

```dart
Future<Map<String, dynamic>> createMembership(
  String teamID, {
  required String email,
  List<String>? roles,
});
```

This is `POST /v1/teams/{teamId}/memberships` with `{ "email": ..., "roles":
[...] }`. The membership is created `invited: true`, `joined: false`, it grants
nothing until accepted:

```json
{
  "$id": "a1b2...",
  "teamId": "6f2b...",
  "teamName": "engineering",
  "userEmail": "grace@example.com",
  "roles": ["developer"],
  "invited": true,
  "joined": false,
  "confirm": false,
  "secret": "7d9f...e0"
}
```

<Callout title="The secret is shown once">
  `secret` is returned only on the create response. Listing memberships never
  includes it. Capture it when you invite; it cannot be read back later.
</Callout>

## Accepting an invite

The invitee, signed in as themselves, redeems the secret. The joining identity
comes from their **session**, never from the request body, so an invite cannot
be redeemed on someone else's behalf. The secret is the credential; the session
says who is joining.

```dart
await client.teams.acceptMembership(teamId, membershipId, secret);
```

```dart
Future<Map<String, dynamic>> acceptMembership(
  String teamID,
  String membershipID,
  String secret,
);
```

This is `PATCH /v1/teams/{teamId}/memberships/{membershipId}/status` with `{
"secret": ... }`. It binds the membership to the current user, marks it
`joined: true`, and clears the one-time secret. If the secret is wrong or the
invite was already used, the call fails with `401` and error code
`membership_invalid_secret`.

## Listing and removing members

```dart
final res = await client.teams.listMemberships(teamId); // GET .../memberships
final members = res['memberships'];

await client.teams.deleteMembership(teamId, membershipId); // DELETE -> 204
```

```dart
Future<Map<String, dynamic>> listMemberships(String teamID);
Future<void> deleteMembership(String teamID, String membershipID);
```

Removing a membership revokes that person's team access immediately: they no
longer resolve the team's roles, so any data permissioned to the team closes to
them.

## Roles

A membership carries a list of `roles` (for example `owner`, `developer`) that
you choose. The team creator is enrolled with the role `owner`. Roles are plain
strings you define for your app; Applad does not attach fixed capabilities to
them beyond turning them into permission roles (below).

## How membership becomes a permission role

This is why teams exist. When a signed-in user makes a request, Applad resolves
their **joined** memberships in the current project and grants, for each team:

- `team:<teamId>`, held by every joined member of the team.
- `team:<teamId>/<role>`, held for each role on that membership, e.g.
  `team:6f2b.../owner`.

A row permissioned `read("team:6f2b...")` therefore admits exactly that team's
members, and `update("team:6f2b.../owner")` admits only its owners. You never
assemble or send these strings from the client; Applad derives them
server-side from the caller's own membership on every request, so they cannot be
forged.

Only **joined** memberships count. An outstanding invite grants nothing until
it is accepted, and a removed member stops resolving the role at once.

See [permissions](/build/permissions) for the full set of permission roles and how to
attach them to data.

## Server-side management

The same operations are available to a backend using a server
[API key](/build/authentication) (header `x-applad-key`), for example to provision a
team from your own signup flow:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/teams \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" \
  -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "engineering"}'
```

A key sees the unscoped team list, and (as noted above) a team it creates has
no owner membership, since there is no user session to enrol.
